title: Affine scalar compatibility of sections of a derived pushforward
statement: Let R,B be commutative rings, X a scheme [def-pc-scheme], f:X→Spec R, g:Spec B→Spec R, and X′ the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put rho=GammaSpec_R.inv followed by g.appTop followed by GammaSpec_B.hom. Let G be sections on X restricted to R along f, H sections on X′ restricted to B along the second projection, DG and DH their global-section right derived functors followed by exact restriction [def-pc-global-derived-rhom], and uG,uH the exact-restriction right-derived comparisons. There exist s:(g_X)* followed by G ≅ H followed by restriction along rho and c:R(g_X)* followed by DG ≅ DH followed by derived exact restriction [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. The map s.hom is identity on every element of sections. For every homotopy complex J, the composite right-derived unit for ((g_X)*,G), followed by uG and c at Qh(J), equals Qh(s.hom on J), followed by the unit for H followed by restriction, and uH. This retains the R action and pins c to the right-derived units; no qcqs, Tor-independence, perfectness, boundedness or quasi-coherence is assumed.

proof.text: Expand the two scalar ring maps. Cancel GammaSpec_B.hom followed by GammaSpec_B.inv and use Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop and pullback.condition. The resulting equality delta composed with alpha = beta composed with rho identifies the two restrictions. Use ModuleCat.restrictScalarsComp and restrictScalarsComp', whiskered by sections on X′, to construct s. Both maps act identically on elements. The direct-image/sections composite is definitionally the same underived restriction composite.

Use isIso_directImage_globalSections_unit_on_kInjective for g_X. The private helper exactComp_unit_isIso uses rightDerivedUnique to compare the unit for global sections followed by exact R restriction with the composite unit; the latter is invertible since exact restriction has invertible unit everywhere and it preserves isomorphisms. Thus the unit for G is invertible on (g_X)*I for every K-injective I. The private helper composite_isRightDerived_of_acyclic uses the K-injective localizer derivability criterion: both factors of the composite unit are invertible on I, so the composite RF followed by RG is itself a right-derived functor.

Let eD:R(F followed by G) ≅ RF followed by RG be rightDerivedUnique. Define c by whiskering uG inverse with RF, then eD inverse, then rightDerivedFunctorNatIso s, then uH. Its sources and targets are exactly DG and DH with the specified restrictions. The rightDerivedNatTrans_app identity for eD says the underived-composite unit followed by eD.hom is the composite unit. Cancel eD.inv and uG.inv in the displayed equation. Apply rightDerivedNatTrans_app to s; the remaining whiskerRight app and Qh.map are definitionally equal. This proves the exact unit equation, for every J, not merely K-injectives.
